newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM says some mines to be sold by May.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM says some mines to be sold by May.

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Tuesday that it expected to sell off some Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines' (ZCCM) assets, including Konkola North and Kansanshi mine, by May 1997.
"I can confirm that Konkola North and Kansanshi mine, and possibly other ZCCM assets, are expected to be handed over to private hands by May this year," a ZCCM spokesman said.
The spokesman declined to release further details, saying a detailed statement would be issued later this week.
On Monday, ZPA chief Valentine Chitalu told reporters that the agency expected to conclude the privatisation of ZCCM by the end of 1998.
"We are moving into the most critical stage of privatisation where we expect parts of ZCCM to go into private hands by the second half of the year," Chitalu said.
"We are confident that the whole programme will proceed on schedule and be completed by the end of 1998," Chitalu added.
ZCCM assets are to be split into 10 different packages for privatisation.
Detailed bids for the packages are expected to be made in February, after which the government will make offers to successful bidders during the course of the year.
The privatisation of ZCCM, which earns around 90 percent of the country's foreign exchange earnings, is seen as crucial to the survival of Zambia's mining industry.
